Control flow

Branching#

si / sin / secus — if, else-if, else.

incipit {
    fixum numerus n ← 2

    si n ≡ 1 {
        nota "one"
    } sin n ≡ 2 {
        nota "two"
    } secus {
        nota "many"
    }
}

One-line branch#

ergo takes a single statement instead of a block. Useful for guards.

functio abs(numerus n) → numerus {
    si n < 0 ergo redde 0 - n
    redde n
}

incipit {
    nota abs(-5)
}

Selecting over a value#

elige picks an arm by value. ceterum is the fallback.

incipit {
    fixum numerus n ← 2

    elige n {
        casu 1 { nota "one" }
        casu 2 { nota "two" }
        ceterum { nota "many" }
    }
}

Matching a union#

discerne matches over a union-typed value. This is how a union hole gets read back out.

incipit {
    fixum numerus ∪ textus valor ← 7

    discerne valor {
        casu 7 { nota "the number seven" }
        casu "x" { nota "the letter x" }
        ceterum { nota "something else" }
    }
}

The difference from elige is intent: elige chooses among values of one type, discerne discriminates among the members of a union.

Returning#

redde returns a value. A function with no → returns nothing and needs no redde.

functio duplica(numerus n) → numerus {
    redde n * 2
}

functio saluta(textus nomen) {
    nota nomen
}

incipit {
    nota duplica(21)
    saluta("Marcus")
}

To exit by the error channel instead, see Errors and catching.
